**Goal:** find drugs bound to tubulin and myosin in real structures, link two
filament genes to their diseases, and draw a heatmap showing which tissue uses
which filament gene.

**Builds on:** [Actin](../actin/lec.qmd), [Microtubules](../microtubules/lec.qmd)
and [Myosin and intermediate filaments](../myosin-if/lec.qmd).
**Time:** about 2 hours.

## Part A: in the browser

No logins are needed. Note your answers as you go; you check them in the
collapsed boxes.

### A1. Taxol on tubulin

Open [PDB 1JFF](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1JFF) (tubulin with taxol). Under
**Macromolecules**, find which chain is α-tubulin and which is β-tubulin. Under
**Small Molecules**, find **TA1** (taxol) and the chain it binds.

**Task A1.** Which chain, and so which tubulin subunit, binds taxol?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**Chain B, β-tubulin.** As in the lecture, taxanes bind β-tubulin inside the
lattice and lock the microtubule.
:::

### A2. Two drugs on the same motor

Open [PDB 5N69](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/5N69) and
[PDB 8QYR](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/8QYR). Both show the motor of
β-cardiac myosin (gene *MYH7*, here from cow) in the same pre-powerstroke state,
each with a different drug. Read each title and the **Small Molecules** list.

**Task A2.** Which entry contains the drug used to treat hypertrophic
cardiomyopathy (HCM), and what is its three-character ligand code?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**8QYR, ligand XB2 (mavacamten)**, an inhibitor that parks myosin heads. 5N69
holds **omecamtiv mecarbil** (code 2OW), an *activator*. Same motor, a shared
binding pocket, opposite effects on force.
:::

### A3. The trial that led to approval

Open the EXPLORER-HCM record,
[NCT03470545](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03470545) on ClinicalTrials.gov.
Find the study **phase** and the **arms** (the groups that were compared).

**Task A3.** Which trial phase is it, and what did the comparison group receive?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**Phase 3**, randomised against **placebo**. You meet trial phases again in the
course on clinical trials and drug development.
:::

### A4. One variant per gene

Open two ClinVar records:
[VCV000014612](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/14612/)
(KRT14 p.Arg125Cys) and
[VCV000014087](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar/variation/14087/)
(MYH7 p.Arg403Gln). Read the **classification** and the **condition(s)**.

**Task A4.** Which disease is linked to each variant?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
KRT14 p.Arg125Cys: **epidermolysis bullosa simplex** (blistering skin).
MYH7 p.Arg403Gln: **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy**. Both are classified
*Pathogenic*. Arg125 sits at the conserved start of the keratin rod, the part
needed for filaments to join end to end.
:::

## Part B: in R

### Before you start

1. Download the template
   [bioinfo-cytoskeleton.Rmd](bioinfo-cytoskeleton.Rmd){download="bioinfo-cytoskeleton.Rmd"}
   into a new folder.
2. Check that `ggplot2`, `jsonlite` and `rmarkdown` are installed
   (`install.packages(c("ggplot2", "jsonlite", "rmarkdown"))` if not).
3. If GTEx is down, set `use_snapshot <- TRUE`. The template then reads the saved
   copy [gtex-expression-2026-11-18.csv](data/gtex-expression-2026-11-18.csv)
   from a `data/` folder next to it, or from this site.

Data: GTEx v8 median TPM (GTEx Portal, open-access summary data), retrieved 2026-11-18.

### What the template does

The given code fetches the median RNA expression (TPM) of 16 cytoskeleton genes
in eight tissues from the GTEx API, and draws an **example heatmap** of raw TPM.
Your job is to complete one `ggplot()` call that draws the same heatmap on a
log scale. Fill the three blanks `___`:

1. **Blank 1:** `fill = log10(tpm + 1)`.
2. **Blank 2:** the layer that draws the tiles (copy it from the example).
3. **Blank 3:** the title of the colour key, `"log10(TPM + 1)"`.

Until all three are filled, the chunk shows an `Error ... unexpected input`.
When they are, you see a 16 × 8 grid of tiles with a colour key titled
**log10(TPM + 1)**, and far more coloured tiles than in the example.

**Task B1.** In the given raw-TPM example, which single tile (gene and tissue)
is brightest?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**DES in skeletal muscle** (about 12 000 TPM; the printed top three confirms it).
Desmin links Z-discs in muscle. Almost every other tile is dark: raw TPM hides
everything below a few hundred, which is why you use a log scale.
:::

**Task B2.** On your log heatmap: in which two tissues is *MYH7* (β-cardiac
myosin, the mavacamten target) high, and which myosin heavy chain is high only in
skeletal muscle?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
*MYH7* is high in **heart (left ventricle) and skeletal muscle** (slow fibres use
the same β-myosin). **MYH2** is high only in skeletal muscle (fast fibres).
:::

**Task B3. [VG]** KRT8 and KRT18 form one keratin pair (type II + type I).
Where are both highest? (a) skin and oesophagus mucosa; (b) liver and lung;
(c) brain cortex and tibial nerve; (d) heart and skeletal muscle.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**(b) liver and lung.** KRT8/KRT18 is the pair of *simple* (single-layer)
epithelia. KRT5/KRT14, the pair broken in epidermolysis bullosa simplex (A4),
marks the *stratified* epithelia of skin and oesophagus.
:::

## Hand in

- Your answers to A1–A4 and B1–B3 (one line each).
- The knitted HTML with both heatmaps and **no errors**.
- The **Data** section showing the retrieval date.
